findings.title: Inverted condition and off-by-one substring indices in isAccessTokenId matcher
findings.body: In `AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId`, the check `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` has two defects that cancel each other out: (1) the encoded prefix has 2-character segments for session type (0..2), token type (2..4), and grant type (4..6), so `substring(3, 5)` slices across the token type and grant type instead of extracting `substring(4, 6)` (and does not check that `items[0].length() == 6`); (2) the `.equals(...)` check is not negated, so it returns `false` on a match rather than a mismatch. Because `substring(3, 5)` (e.g. `"ta"` for `"onrtac"`) never equals the expected grant shortcut, the matcher currently passes for any 2-part token ID regardless of the actual grant shortcut.

findings.title: Constructor validates grantType twice instead of rawTokenId
findings.body: In the `AccessTokenContext` constructor, line 73 calls `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed");` instead of `Objects.requireNonNull(rawTokenId, "Null rawTokenId not allowed");`. A null `rawTokenId` will bypass this check and be stored on the instance, resulting in `"...:null"` when encoded.

findings.title: testIncorrectGrantType catches NullPointerException instead of testing IllegalArgumentException
findings.body: In `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderTest.before()`, `factory.postInit(...)` is not called, leaving `factory.sessionFactory` null. When `testIncorrectGrantType` calls `provider.getTokenContextFromTokenId("ofrtac:5678")`, `factory.getGrantTypeByShortcut("ac")` misses the map and dereferences the null `sessionFactory`, throwing a `NullPointerException`. Because the test catches `RuntimeException` rather than asserting `IllegalArgumentException`, the `NullPointerException` is silently ignored and the unknown-grant-type error handling in `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId` is never exercised.

findings.title: OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut() Javadoc specifies 3-letter shortcuts while encoder requires 2 characters
findings.body: The Javadoc on `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut()` states `@return usually like 3-letters shortcut of specific grants`, whereas `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId` requires the total encoded context to be 6 characters and extracts the grant shortcut from indices 4..6 (exact length of 2). Any grant type factory implementing a 3-letter shortcut per the Javadoc will produce 7-character prefixes in `encodeTokenId` that fail decoding with `IllegalArgumentException("Incorrect token id: '...'. Expected length of 6.")`.
